judgment.rationale: Display timeout on the lock screen is documented behavior, not evidence that Awake stopped working. The difficult dock wake-up is a separate symptom needing a controlled Awake-disabled comparison; do not change lock-screen policy to mask it.
evidence: PowerToys0.102.3001 on Windows11; the report expects displays to stay on at the lock screen and also reports difficult wake-up through a dock.

The official Awake documentation explicitly states that Keep screen on applies only while unlocked; locking restores Windows display timeout while the system keep-awake mode continues.

title: Awake not working anymore after powertoys update

comment.body: Awake intentionally stops keeping the display on while Windows is locked, even with Keep screen on enabled; see https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/powertoys/awake#lock-screen-behavior. The attachment already supplied is noted; no repeat upload is requested. The difficulty waking the docked displays is a separate concern: with the same dock/display setup, does one lock/unlock still require reconnecting the dock when Awake is disabled? Please compare enabled versus disabled and state the wake-up delay in each case.
